novel_mechanics_found: Level 3 introduces a previously absent color-11 B glyph at the top of a vertically anchored E-9-8-C chain. Actions 1/2 move the color-6 patterned actuator vertically and actions 4/3 extend or retract its patterned horizontal body. In the earlier banked levels, colored blocks can ride vertically on the body and contiguous rows shift together; the level-3 B-anchored column resisted the same pull, lift, merge, and row-reversal constructions. Direct ACTION6 clicks on both glyphs and ACTION5 produced no visible selection or release effect at the tested rendered coordinates.
narrative: The 44-action resolver prefix was replayed first and reached levels_completed=2. I reconstructed the prior transition mechanics from rendered frames, then tried direct probes, the prior level's 30-action construction, several scaled row-reversal plans, and explicit interaction with the unexplained B glyph. None advanced level 3; multiple superficially analogous plans ended with the anchored vertical column unchanged. I stopped with 35 steps unspent because no candidate win had been observed and retained enough budget to run the mandatory fresh-reset reproduction gate, which passed for level 2.
gotchas: frame.frame is an animation stack for this game; inspect its final 64x64 slice rather than treating the full stack as one grid.
The color-6 actuator begins one grid cell farther left on level 3 than on the first banked level, so horizontal action counts do not transfer literally.
A horizontal body may visually overlap a colored 4x4 block without moving it; color-count changes caused by overlay are not evidence that the block was detached or collected.
The first two levels contain no visible B glyph, while level 3 does; treating the new vertical column as an ordinary unanchored block row led to repeatable no-progress loops.
ACTION6 clicks at the rendered centers/corners of B and the color-6 glyph, and an ACTION5 probe, caused no visible mode change in this session.
